tasks.short: Inform citizens of community services and recommend options.

steps.what: Read which community services fit this citizen's problem.
inputs: the citizen's problem as the officer heard it
services card when the community-services colleague has written one
outputs: the community services that fit this problem

steps.what: Inform citizens of those community services and recommend options to facilitate longer-term problem resolution.
inputs: the community services that fit this problem
outputs: the options the officer recommended for longer-term problem resolution

tasks.design: The community-services colleague keeps a paper services card: the problem, the service, who to contact, and what the service does not do. The patrol officer reads that card, or the posted services list when a row is missing, then informs the citizen and recommends options in person. The recommendation stays the officer's.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which service fits sat in old leaflets, so each conversation started as a search. The citizen's problem is heard only in the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: The community-services colleague already knows the contact and the limit of each service. Writing the current rows on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the problem, choosing which option to recommend, and saying it to the citizen stay with the officer.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which option fits this person's longer-term problem, from what they say in the conversation.
tasks.altitude: Finding the service and the contact is shorter when the card is current. The officer still informs the citizen and still recommends the option.

reach.task: Keep the services card for problems citizens bring to a patrol officer
reach.learn: To name the problem, the service, who to contact, and what the service does not do, and to drop a row that is no longer true

evidence.claim: Informing a citizen and recommending a community service is a conversation. A card shortens finding the contact. It does not hear the problem or make the recommendation. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one citizen and one problem. Informing and recommending keep their full time.

Services card fields are problem, service, who to contact, and what the service does not do. The producer is the community-services colleague, when a service or a contact changes. If a row is missing or stale, the officer reads the posted services list inside the lookup. Which option to recommend comes from the conversation in s2, not from the card.
No records screen is in this design. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the community-services colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 officer hours on this task. The officer's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a small post has a community-services colleague, or the officer keeps the card.
How often the right service is one the posted list does not name.
research_questions: Of the citizen conversations in a month, how many are answered by a current services card, and how many change because of what the citizen says?

incremental.description: The patrol officer adds no recurring chore. Reading the card and informing the citizen stay in the steps above.
The community-services colleague writes the services card by hand when a service or a contact changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the services card has no row, the officer reads the posted services list inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Informing the citizen and recommending an option never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise jail staff, officers and deputy sheriffs.

steps.what: Read the shift notes for enforcement staff, officers and deputy sheriffs.
inputs: duty card when the duty colleague has written one
outputs: who is on duty and what was handed over

steps.what: Supervise the jail staff, officers and deputy sheriffs on that enforcement shift.
inputs: who is on duty and what was handed over
the jail staff, officers and deputy sheriffs on the shift
outputs: the supervision given on that shift

tasks.design: The duty colleague keeps a paper duty card: the post, who is on duty, and what was handed over. The patrol officer reads that card, or the posted duty list when a row is missing, then supervises the jail staff, officers and deputy sheriffs in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Who was on the last shift sat in a handover note, so each shift started as a search. What staff need next is visible only while supervising.
tasks.enabler_now: The duty colleague already holds the handover. Writing the current post, names and handover on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Supervising the shift, and deciding what to say to staff, stay with the officer.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing who is struggling on this shift and what to do about it, in the room.
tasks.altitude: Finding who is on duty is shorter when the card is current. The officer still supervises the shift.

reach.task: Keep the duty card for each enforcement shift
reach.learn: To name the post, who is on duty, and what was handed over, and to drop a row when the shift ends

evidence.claim: Supervising jail staff, officers and deputy sheriffs is time in the room. A duty card shortens finding who is on duty. It does not supervise. Model knowledge.
Dutch works-council law requires consent before an arrangement that watches how staff work. This task adds no such arrangement. The officer still supervises in person.

assumptions: The boundary is one shift of jail staff, officers and deputy sheriffs. Supervising keeps its full time.

Duty card fields are post, who is on duty, and what was handed over. The producer is the duty colleague, at each handover. If a row is missing or stale, the officer reads the posted duty list inside the lookup. What to say to staff comes from supervising in s2, not from the card.
No records screen is in this design. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the duty colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 officer hours on this task. The officer's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a small post has a duty colleague, or the outgoing officer writes the card.
How much of this task is a sergeant's work rather than a patrol officer's.
research_questions: Of the shifts in a month, how many start from a current duty card, and how many change because of what the officer sees while supervising?

incremental.description: The patrol officer adds no recurring chore. Reading the duty card and supervising the shift stay in the steps above.
The duty colleague writes the duty card by hand at each handover.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the duty card has no row, the officer reads the posted duty list inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Supervising the shift never shrinks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Process prisoners and keep booking and status records.

steps.what: Process the prisoners at this booking.
inputs: the prisoner brought in for booking
outputs: the prisoner processed at this booking
the number the officer took at booking

steps.what: Read the prisoner status already recorded for this booking.
inputs: the number the officer took at booking
status card when the custody colleague has written one
outputs: the prisoner status already on the card

steps.what: Prepare and maintain the records of prisoner bookings and status during the pre-trial process.
inputs: the prisoner processed at this booking
the prisoner status already on the card
outputs: the booking record the officer wrote for this pre-trial process

tasks.design: The custody colleague keeps a paper status card: the number the officer already holds, the status, where the person is held, and the next court date. The patrol officer processes the prisoner, reads that card or the last booking note when a row is missing, then prepares and maintains the booking record by hand.
tasks.previous_blocker: The status already on file sat in an earlier note, so each booking started with a search. Processing the person and writing this record cannot be skipped.
tasks.enabler_now: The custody colleague already knows the status and the next court date. Writing them on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Processing the prisoner, and preparing and maintaining this booking record, stay with the officer.
tasks.human_edge: Checking the person in front of them against the number, and writing the booking record that will be used later.
tasks.altitude: Finding the status already on file is shorter when the card is current. The officer still processes the prisoner and still writes the booking record.

reach.task: Keep the status card for people already in custody
reach.learn: To name the number, the status, where the person is held, and the next court date, and to drop a row when the status changes

evidence.claim: Processing a prisoner and writing the booking record are the officer's own work. A status card shortens finding the status already on file. It does not process the person or write the record. Model knowledge.

Dutch police-data law requires a person before a solely automated decision with adverse effect, and keeps daily-task data for at most five years. This task adds no automated decision and sets no new retention period. The officer writes the booking record by hand.

assumptions: The boundary is one prisoner and one booking in the pre-trial process. Processing the person and writing the record each keep their full time.

Status card fields are the number the officer already took, the status, where the person is held, and the next court date. The producer is the custody colleague, when a status changes. The card exists before this booking note is written. If a row is missing or stale, the officer reads the last booking note inside the lookup. The identity comes from processing the person in s1, not from the card.
The record in s3 is a new note the officer writes. It is not the card s2 reads. No records screen is in this design. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the custody colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 officer hours on this task. The officer's own upkeep is zero because writing the record is already s3.
unknowns: Whether a small post has a custody colleague, or the same officer holds the earlier status note.
Which booking facts a later court file must repeat in the officer's own handwriting.
research_questions: Of the bookings in a month, how many find the prior status on a current card, and how many need the last booking note because the card has no row?

incremental.description: The patrol officer adds no recurring chore. Processing the prisoner and writing the booking record stay in the steps above.
The custody colleague writes the status card by hand when a status or a court date changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the status card has no row, the officer reads the last booking note inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Processing the prisoner and writing the booking record never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Locate and confiscate property under a court order.

steps.what: Read the court order that directed which personal property to locate.
inputs: order card when the records colleague has copied one
outputs: the personal property the court order directed the officer to locate

steps.what: Locate that personal property and confiscate it as the court order directed.
inputs: the personal property the court order directed the officer to locate
outputs: the personal property the officer located and confiscated

tasks.design: The records colleague copies onto a paper order card the case, the property, where it was last known, and what the court order directs. The patrol officer reads that card, or the paper order when a row is missing, then locates the property and confiscates it in person. The court wrote the order. The officer carries it out.
tasks.previous_blocker: The property line sat inside a long court order, so each job started as a search. Finding the goods and taking them is work on site.
tasks.enabler_now: The records colleague can copy the four fields the officer needs. That copy needs no new system and no model. The order itself already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Locating the property and confiscating it, as the order directs, stay with the officer.
tasks.human_edge: Matching the goods on site to the property the order names, and taking only that.
tasks.altitude: Finding the property line in the order is shorter when the card is current. The officer still locates the property and still confiscates it.

reach.task: Copy the property line from each court order onto an order card
reach.learn: To name the case, the property, where it was last known, and what the order directs, and to copy only what the order says

evidence.claim: Locating and confiscating property under a court order is work on site. A copied property line shortens finding that line in the order. It does not find the goods or take them. Model knowledge.
Dutch police-data law requires a person before a solely automated decision with adverse effect. Confiscation here is the officer acting on a court order. This task adds no automated decision.

assumptions: The boundary is one court order and the personal property it names. Locating and confiscating keep their full time.

Order card fields are case, property, where last known, and what the order directs. The court wrote the order before this task. The producer of the card is the records colleague, who copies those fields by hand. If a row is missing or stale, the officer reads the paper order inside the lookup. What to take is what the order says, checked on site in s2.
No records screen is in this design. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the records colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 officer hours on this task. The officer's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a small post has a records colleague, or the officer reads the order with no card.
How often the goods are not at the last known place, so the card's location line is wrong.
research_questions: Of the court orders in a month, how many have a current property line on the card, and how many still need the paper order because the card has no row?

incremental.description: The patrol officer adds no recurring chore. Reading the order and confiscating the property stay in the steps above.
The records colleague copies the order card by hand when a court order arrives.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the order card has no row, the officer reads the paper order inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Locating the property and confiscating it never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The patrol officer still informs the citizen, supervises the shift, processes the prisoner, writes the booking record, and locates and confiscates the property. A current card only shortens finding a service, a duty note, a status, or the order's property line.
reach: A community-services colleague learns to name the problem, the service, who to contact, and what the service does not do before the officer informs a citizen.
A duty colleague learns to name the post, who is on duty, and what was handed over before the officer supervises the shift.
A custody colleague learns to name the number, the status, where the person is held, and the next court date before the officer writes the booking record.
A records colleague learns to copy the case, the property, where it was last known, and what the court order directs before the officer locates it.
skills_to_grow: Open the posted services list, the posted duty list, the last booking note, or the paper order when the card has no row.
Recommend the service, supervise the shift, write the booking entry, and confiscate from what the officer sees and the order says, not from the card alone.
role.ambitious_version: The officer still informs, recommends, supervises, processes, writes the booking record, and confiscates. The cards do not.
